newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India fight back led by Azharuddhin century.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India fight back led by Azharuddhin century.

text.p: A stirring eight-wicket stand of 141 runs between Mohammad Azharuddin and Anil Kumble led India's fight back against South Africa on the third day of the second test at Calcutta on Friday.
The pair put on 150 runs in just two hours to lunch with a display of scintillating strokes, scuttling the visitors' hopes of bowling India out and enforcing the follow-on.
India's first innings ended at 329 shortly after lunch having gone into the interval at 320 for seven.

The home side began the day at 161 for seven, requiring 68 runs to make South Africa bat again with only three wickets in hand. Overnight batsman Javagal Srinath did not last long and was bowled by Allan Donald for 11.

Azharuddin, who retired hurt on Thursday after being hit on the arm by Brian McMillan, then walked in to play one of the finest innings seen at Eden Gardens, scoring a well-deserved century in the process.
Peppered by short-pitched deliveries by the South Africans seeking to expose his weakness against the short rising ball, Azharuddin unleashed a series of pulls to demoralise the opposition.
